subject: Pilot pricing — stair-step incentives & SLA layering
messages:
From: Samira Patel <samira@cortexa.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot pricing inquiry — incentive structure options

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Cortexa is keen to run a short 6-week pilot focused on summarization and intent classification. Two quick asks from my side before we lock dates:

1) Can you outline an incentive structure that lets us try higher throughput in weeks 3–4 without committing to a long-term seat license? We want a path that doesn't penalize burst usage during integration.

2) What SLA guarantees do you offer for latency during the pilot, and is there a mechanism to layer a higher SLA for a narrow critical path (webhooks/real-time inference) while keeping the bulk at standard SLOs?

Attached is a one-page scope. Happy to jump on a call.

Best,
Samira
Director of ML Platforms
Cortexa
Attachment: Cortexa_Pilot_SOW_v1.pdf (application/pdf)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Samira Patel <samira@cortexa.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-20T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot pricing inquiry — incentive structure options

Hi Samira — great to meet you too, and thanks for the scope.

Short answer to both:

- Incentive/packaging: We can offer a stair-step (tiered) pricing for the pilot where the first 2 weeks are a reduced-rate evaluation band, weeks 3–4 are a mid-tier band that includes a temporary burst cap upgrade, and weeks 5–6 convert to a top-tier trial rate up to a capped usage level. If you exceed the mid-tier cap during the burst window we can either (a) apply overage at the mid-tier rate or (b) temporarily enable an add-on burst pool that draws from a pre-authorized credit (your chosen option). This keeps you flexible without requiring seat licenses.

- SLA layering: Yes — we support per-route SLA policies. For the pilot we can guarantee 99th percentile latency for standard batch endpoints and offer a premium webhook/realtime route with a tighter latency SLO and priority routing. This will be scoped in the SOW as "Critical-path SLA" and priced as a small uplift during active windows.

I'll attach a short example pricing sketch and a few options for conversion incentives (commit credits vs. one-time migration credit). Marissa and Kim are cc'd for the formal SOW and legal checklist.

Would Thursday 10 AM PT work to walk through the options?

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachment: usage-projection.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Liam O'Neal <liam.oneal@cortexa.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Samira Patel <samira@cortexa.com>
Date: 2026-10-21T08:19:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot pricing inquiry — incentive structure options

Karthik,

Thursday works. A couple of additional finance asks ahead of the call:

- Can we get a clear definition of what counts toward the "mid-tier" cap (all tokens vs. served requests vs. inference time)? Cortexa procurement wants to avoid surprise billings.
- If Cortexa converts to Dedicated after pilot, will any unused pilot credits roll into the initial committed tranche, or are they forfeited?

Also — any flexibility on deferring the first invoice until after week 3 if the burst test is a gating factor for our QA team?

Thanks,
Liam
Sr. Finance Manager
Cortexa

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, samira@cortexa.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-22T16:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot pricing inquiry — incentive structure options

Thanks for the notes, all.

Quick answers/plans from Redwood finance and legal:

- Mid-tier cap unit: defined as "billable inference units" (per-request token count normalized to inference units). We'll include the exact normalization table in the SOW. That avoids token vs request disputes.

- Conversion credit: We can apply up to 50% of unused pilot credits toward the first 3 months of a Dedicated commit (subject to a minimum three‑month commit). The remaining 50% may be applied as one-time migration credits if you choose a 12‑month Dedicated contract. This is our standard conversion ladder for pilots and is intended to reduce friction.

- Invoice deferral: We can defer invoicing until after week 3 subject to a write-off exposure limit (small pre-authorized card hold for up to $5k). If you need a PO-first flow we can accommodate but would require procurement timelines to be finalized before pilot start.

I'll update the SOW with these clauses and circulate for DocuSign. Karthish — I'll need the usage-projection.xlsx filled with expected peak QPS for the burst windows before I finalize the SLA routing pricing.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
